title: Steam over a boiling chamber: opaque, translucent, or thinned by fill
question: Which one lets you still read the pool underneath without the steam stopping looking like steam?
context_md:
The pending `GasMode` default. Three modes behind `;` in the app, `Opaque` today. `filmstrip scene=boil` at frames 250, 370, 490 -- the steam fills the chamber, which is exactly the case that motivated the selector: drawn opaque the sheet becomes a speckled wall with the pool somewhere behind it.

`ByFill` keys the alpha on the cell's own `aux`, which for steam is the water it is carrying, so a plume that has thinned out draws thinner -- it is a readout as well as a look.

Both alternatives change the same 24,704 pixels against Opaque; they differ in how far (mean |dRGB| 35.7 for Translucent against 40.2 for ByFill), so this is genuinely a look question and not a does-it-fire one.

items.label: C
items.caption: ByFill -- alpha follows the water the steam carries
